facts.fact: Three-month type 2 diabetes follow-up.
Dietary lapses over the holidays (more bread and sweets).
Takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily but misses the evening dose three or four times a week.
Metformin causes cramping and loose stools about an hour after a dose.
Morning home glucose readings usually 8 to 10.
Walks about twice a week, less since the weather got cold.
No chest pain.
No eye exam in about two years.
Night-time tingling in the toes of both feet.
Has not started cinnamon supplements; advised against them.
A1c 8.1%, up from 7.4% in the spring.
Blood pressure 142/88.
Weight 98 kg, up 2 kg since the last visit.
Foot pulses normal; monofilament sensation reduced at both great toes.
Type 2 diabetes with worsening glycemic control.
Findings consistent with early diabetic peripheral neuropathy.
Blood pressure above target.
Switch metformin to extended-release, 1000 mg twice daily, for GI tolerance.
Start empagliflozin 10 mg once daily; counselled on genital yeast infections, urination and hydration.
Refer to the diabetes education program and a dietitian.
Refer to an eye doctor for a retinal exam.
Kidney function and urine test today.
Recheck blood pressure next visit; start medication if still above 130/80.
Repeat A1c in three months; daily foot checks and call about any sores.
